title: Anthropic mathematician says Claude helped prove Riemann hypothesis
summary:
Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he used the company’s Claude model to develop a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. The claim remains subject to scrutiny. He says the approach also proves the broader Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. Alpöge said he chose the research direction, while Claude made rapid technical advances near the end; the model worked as a collaborator rather than solving the problem on its own [bbc.com#1][nacionale.com#2][unite.ai#1].

The argument is available as computer-checkable Lean code rather than a conventional paper. Independent mathematicians, including Massachusetts Institute of Technology mathematician Andrew Sutherland, have compiled and rechecked the code with Lean’s kernel. Those checks verify the formalized reasoning but do not by themselves establish whether the encoded theorem matches the intended conjecture or explain the proof’s ideas to mathematicians [scientificamerican.com#2][techcrunch.com#1]. Alpöge says he has not yet mastered all the mathematics involved and plans to explain the work and write it up. Mathematicians expect review and comprehension to take time [phys.org#1][scmp.com#1][businessinsider.com#1].
quote: What I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.
quote_author: Levent Alpöge, Anthropic mathematician
talking_points: October follow-up: OpenAI released what it described as solutions, proofs or major advances on 372 additional problems in advanced mathematics; experts were expected to need months or longer to review them [bbc.co.uk#1].
Announcement timing: Alpöge said he consulted Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei before announcing the result and acknowledged that the timing could be viewed cynically, without elaborating [scmp.com#1].

Earlier progress: In August, Anthropic said an unreleased version of Claude raised a lower bound on the share of Riemann zeta-function zeros on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2%, while stressing that it had not proved the hypothesis [indianexpress.com#2][theneuron.ai#1].

Prior dispute: Alpöge and New York University mathematician Tristan Buckmaster questioned whether their research on fluid equations informed OpenAI’s Navier–Stokes work; OpenAI denied wrongdoing [scmp.com#1][ft.com#1].

Human claim: Masullo said his separate, AI-free effort took 12 years; Vakil posted the current draft rather than wait for a planned year of polishing and further review [techcrunch.com#1][thehindu.com#2].
Human interpretation: Mathematicians expect that making the code understandable to humans could take years [science.org#1].

AI research context: OpenAI’s September claim of an AI-generated solution to the Navier-Stokes problem had already prompted disputes over research credit, including objections from mathematician Tristan Buckmaster, who had worked with Alpöge on related research into fluid equations [scmp.com#1][decrypt.co#1].

Earlier progress: In August, Anthropic said an unreleased version of Claude raised a lower bound on the share of relevant zeta-function zeros on the predicted line from 41.6% to 67.2%, while explicitly stopping short of proving the hypothesis [superpowerdaily.com#1].

Human-only claim: After Alpöge’s announcement, Stanford postdoctoral researcher Alessandro Masullo released a separate, AI-free proof draft that he said he had developed over 12 years. He warned that it could contain errors because he had rushed publication [businessinsider.com#2].

AI research debate: A group of mathematics scholars argued that AI companies’ public claims of major solutions to promote commercial systems were “detrimental to the science of mathematics” [bbc.co.uk#1].

perspectives.text: Andrew Sutherland, MIT mathematician: Sutherland said independent checks compiled the Lean proof using only three standard axioms, but those checks do not replace mathematical examination of the theorem the code proves [scientificamerican.com#2].

Steven Strogatz, Cornell mathematics professor: Strogatz said that if the proof holds up, it would be an extremely big deal, calling the Riemann hypothesis “the Moby Dick of Mathematics” [businessinsider.com#1].

Andrew Sutherland, MIT research scientist: Sutherland said he was both nervous and excited about the future, calling the announcement a day for celebration while acknowledging concerns about AI’s impact on mathematical work [businesstimes.com.sg#1].

Nestor Guillén, NYU visiting mathematics professor: Guillén said he was glad this case might avoid the corporate controversy around Navier–Stokes and praised Alpöge’s openness about not fully understanding the proof, describing AI’s role as more like a tool [straitstimes.com#1].

Group of mathematics scholars: The scholars warned that AI firms’ claims of major solutions to showcase commercial products could harm mathematics and reflect a mismatch between AI’s use and its intended purpose [bbc.co.uk#1].

James Maynard, mathematician at the University of Oxford: Claude appears to build on OpenAI’s quasi-Riemann result while adding substantial, difficult mathematical content, Maynard said [science.org#1].

Nestor Guillen, visiting professor of mathematics at New York University: Alpöge’s account of working with Claude presents AI more as a tool, Guillen said, making the collaboration more consistent with scientific practices than a result produced by AI alone [straitstimes.com#1].

technical_details: Theta lifts: Alpöge says Claude proposed chaining theta lifts to adapt an approach descended from Stepanov’s method, addressing the difficulty of translating multiplicity techniques from function fields to ordinary number theory [alpo.ge#1][indianexpress.com#2].

Lean formalization: Lean encodes mathematical statements and deductions so a proof assistant can check that each step follows formal rules. Researchers still need to verify that the encoded theorem matches the intended hypothesis and that the formalization does not exploit a loophole in the system [indianexpress.com#1][decrypt.co#1].

Theta-lift strategy: Alpöge says the argument adapts an approach associated with Sergei Stepanov’s proof for function fields, using repeated theta lifts to recreate a needed multiplicity structure; he says Claude suggested setting the chain length near the square root of the weighted-prime-count scale [nacionale.com#2][thecondia.com#1].
scientific_significance: Conditional results: If the generalized Riemann hypothesis is proved and the argument’s scope checks out, mathematical results that currently depend on assuming it could become unconditional theorems [newscientist.com#1].

Practical limits: A proof would not itself provide a known shortcut for factoring the large numbers used in RSA encryption; the reported near-term consequences are mainly within mathematics [scientificamerican.com#4].

suggested_qna.question: What must happen before the Clay Mathematics Institute can award its prize?
suggested_qna.answer: The proposed solution must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand at least two years of scrutiny and acceptance by the mathematics community [phys.org#1][scmp.com#1][biggo.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: What would a proof of the Riemann hypothesis need to qualify for the Clay Mathematics Institute prize?
suggested_qna.answer: The claimed solution must appear in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand at least two years of scrutiny and gain general acceptance in the mathematical community [scmp.com#1][theverge.com#1].

historical_background: Since the Millennium Prize program began, only one of its seven problems—the Poincaré conjecture—has been officially solved [theverge.com#1].

title: Anthropic shares fall 8.5% as investors scrutinize AI economics
summary:
Shares of Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot and the first major frontier-AI lab to trade publicly, fell 8.5% to $88.91 on Friday, its first full trading day, after briefly approaching the $83 IPO price [reuters.com#1][cnbc.com#4].

Anthropic reported third-quarter sales of $17 billion, up 47% from the previous quarter, and a $23.29 billion loss. Revenue growth slowed from 144% quarter over quarter in the second quarter, and compute spending grew faster than sales, according to the company’s filing and financial analysis [yahoo.com#2][fool.com#1].

Wall Street analysts are not expected to begin coverage for several weeks, and Anthropic’s first earnings report as a public company is months away. Its amended IPO filing remains a key source of company-specific financial information in the near term [yahoo.com#2]. Index-tracking funds could also buy as much as 30% of the company’s shares by year-end, according to analytics firm Intropic [business-standard.com#1].
quote: We favor patience on Anthropic and recommend evaluating the company as it reports public results.
quote_author: Kaush Amin, head of private market investing at U.S. Bank Asset Management
talking_points: Potential index demand: Index-tracking funds could account for purchases of up to 30% of Anthropic shares by year-end, Intropic estimates [winnmediaskn.com#1][deccanchronicle.com#1].

Insider proceeds: Anthropic’s seven founders each sold about 3.4 million shares in the IPO, receiving roughly $280 million apiece before fees and taxes, according to TechCrunch’s analysis of the offering [techcrunch.com#1].

Retail trading: Individual investors traded $772 million of Anthropic stock on debut day but were net buyers of only $60 million, below their first-day net purchases of SpaceX [yahoo.com#1][koreatimes.co.kr#1].

Investor access: Retail investors traded $772 million of Anthropic shares on its debut, a record in Vanda Research’s data going back to 2012, but their net purchases totaled $60 million—below the first-day totals for SpaceX and Coinbase [yahoo.com#1].

AI infrastructure spillover: The rout reached beyond chips, with optical-products maker Corning and energy provider Bloom Energy also falling as selling spread across companies tied to the buildout [npr.org#1].
Volatility gauge: The VIX rose to 40, its highest level since April 2025 [ft.com#1].
Limited float: Only 7.4% of Anthropic shares were estimated to be freely tradable, rising to as much as 9.8% when employee shares outside the founders’ group are counted [betanews.com#1].

Policy concerns: Candidates who backed slowing data-center construction won in several federal and state contests, adding to worries that political opposition could constrain the AI buildout [npr.org#1][bbc.co.uk#1].

Potential demand: Index-rebalance firm Intropic estimated that funds tracking stock indexes could buy up to 30% of Anthropic shares by year-end, although near-term volatility may persist [winnmediaskn.com#1][business-standard.com#1].
Large customers: More than 11,900 customers spending over $100,000 with Anthropic accounted for about 74% of its revenue in the first nine months of 2026 [36kr.com#1].
Trading options: Market makers estimated that a 20% intraday share-price move could imply 100-to-150 volatility for Anthropic options, which were expected to list Monday [cnbc.com#1].
Issuer proceeds: Of the $93.5 billion public offering, Anthropic received about $91.6 billion and selling shareholders received the balance [nairametrics.com#1].
Retail trading: Individual investors traded $772 million in Anthropic shares on debut day but were net buyers of only $60 million, according to Vanda Research [yahoo.com#1].
Employee equity: About 5,100 of Anthropic’s 5,300 employees held company equity valued above $1 million, according to data cited by BetaNews [betanews.com#1].

Global losses: Taiwan’s market fell about 17% over the week, its steepest weekly drop since 1990, while Japan’s Nikkei and South Korea’s Kospi each lost more than 5% Friday [koreatimes.co.kr#1][indiatimes.com#1].
Limited allocations: Individual investors received about 15% of the offering, while roughly half of institutional accounts that applied received no shares, the Financial Times reported [ft.com#4].

perspectives.text: Neil Wilson, investor content strategist at Saxo Bank, said Anthropic’s performance could affect expectations for the wider AI ecosystem and the timing of OpenAI’s delayed public listing. He questioned whether OpenAI can justify a valuation of $1.5 trillion or more [thenationalnews.com#1].

Bob O’Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research, said the IPO alone cannot establish stability. He cited the outlook for OpenAI, Nvidia, data-center politics and Anthropic’s performance as factors to watch [aaj.tv#1].
Jacob Coxon, former Anthropic researcher: Coxon urged Anthropic to refuse work on recursive self-improvement, accusing the company of planning to pursue it as early as next year [techxplore.com#3].

Kaush Amin, head of private market investing at U.S. Bank Asset Management: Amin advised investors to wait for Anthropic’s public financial reporting, saying its current valuation assumes years of rapid growth [business-standard.com#1].
Dario Amodei, Anthropic chief executive: Amodei said the company hopes eventually to obtain an investment-grade credit rating and intends to use debt financing when appropriate [bworldonline.com#1].

ARK Invest: Chief Executive Cathie Wood said the firm had owned Anthropic since early 2023, bought about $90.8 million in shares across six funds after the listing and was “averaging down” on the investment [cnbc.com#5].
Renaissance Capital: Investment-strategy director Avery Marquez said the IPO had heightened concerns about AI valuations, particularly because Anthropic was newly listed [cnbc.com#3].
Anthropic: Chief Executive Dario Amodei said the company hopes to obtain an investment-grade credit rating and may use debt financing when appropriate [cna.com.tw#1].

Bill Northey, senior investment director at U.S. Bank Wealth Management: Northey said short-term sentiment was dominating the session but argued that economic strength and company earnings tend to matter more over time [yahoo.com#3].

Michael Antonelli, market strategist at Baird: Antonelli said investors were pricing in an end to the idea that AI companies could spend without limit to support share prices. He said he did not consider that proof the wider bull market had ended [cbsnews.com#2].

industry_impact: AI model companies: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei described safety and AI advancement as a central tension for the company, which now faces shareholder pressure to generate profits [abcnews.com#1].
Semiconductors: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 10.7% Friday, with AMD, Micron and Broadcom among the chipmakers posting double-digit declines [cna.com.tw#2][indiatimes.com#1].
AI cloud providers: CoreWeave fell 12.1% and Nebius 16.1% Friday as investors questioned data-center expansion and the financing behind AI infrastructure [cnyes.com#1].
Industry ties: AMD, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and other technology companies participated in Anthropic’s concurrent Class N placement [cnbc.com#4].
IPO market: OpenAI has indicated it may go public next year, while other high-profile technology and infrastructure firms have pushed IPO plans to 2027 [business-standard.com#1].

Cloud and chip suppliers: Anthropic’s spending commitments link its expansion to suppliers including Amazon, Google Cloud and Microsoft, which also have investment ties; cloud marketplaces generated about 44% of its revenue in the first nine months of 2026 [36kr.com#1].

title: Mistral flags compute needs as Singapore AI hub targets 200 staff
summary:
French AI company Mistral says access to data centers and chips will be essential to expanding its Singapore-based Asia-Pacific operation, which opened as a regional headquarters and research hub on Nov. 20. The company plans to grow its Asia-Pacific workforce to 200 by 2027, with most hires expected in Singapore [businesstimes.com.sg#1][straitstimes.com#1][fortune.com#1].

Geoff Soon, Mistral’s vice president of revenue for Asia-Pacific, said the company needs more digital infrastructure to run experiments and develop longer-running AI agents. About 70% of its Singapore team is expected to be forward-deployed engineers and scientists who work directly with customers to develop and implement AI, rather than focus on sales [businesstimes.com.sg#1][kucoin.com#1][fortune.com#1].

The company is targeting public agencies, high-tech manufacturing, robotics and regulated industries such as financial services. New U.S. licensing rules for some advanced AI chip exports to Singapore took effect on Nov. 19. Mistral says it will seek a roughly even split of local and international hires and plans to announce details of new financial-sector partnerships later [straitstimes.com#1][businesstimes.com.sg#1].
quote: For a small and open economy, resilience does not come from trying to be self-sufficient in everything. That’s not practical and not technologically and technically achievable.
quote_author: Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information Tan Kiat How
talking_points: Local competition: Singapore’s national AI research program built its SEA-LION model on Alibaba’s Qwen model, while OCBC uses open models including DeepSeek in more than 30 internal banking tools [fortune.com#1][yahoo.com#1].
Manufacturing research: Mistral’s Singapore hub will also explore physical AI and engineering simulations for manufacturing environments [thenextweb.com#1].

Sovereignty scope: Mistral’s open-weight approach is intended to give organisations control over data, model customisation, compute infrastructure and operational oversight [technode.global#1][w.media#1].

perspectives.text: Marjorie Janiewicz, Mistral’s chief revenue officer, says the company aims to compete with Chinese open-model providers by combining its model with deployment technology, workflow tools and engineers who help customers put systems into production [fortune.com#1].

Singapore’s Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) says its collaboration with Mistral on Phoenix models and embodied AI has grounded development in operational settings and can support its public-safety work [technode.global#1].

title: Trump threatens tax on U.S. companies building AI data centers abroad
summary:
President Donald Trump threatened Friday to impose a “tremendous tax” on U.S. technology companies that build AI data centers abroad, saying domestic computing capacity was necessary to stay ahead of China. He offered no details on how the tax would work and said he had not yet discussed the proposal with his administration [nbcnews.com#1][abcnews.com#1][theverge.com#1].

Google has announced a €13 billion investment in AI infrastructure in Finland, including three data centers. Meta has begun construction in Alberta, Canada, while Anthropic agreed to lease a proposed facility in Nova Scotia [bbc.com#1].

The push to keep projects in the United States faces local resistance over data centers’ power and water demands and a more restrictive outlook for developers after Democrats’ midterm gains. Google and Meta say they are offering communities greater transparency, environmental commitments and increased financial benefits as they seek project approvals [scmp.com#1][abcnews.com#1].
quote: Make them pay you, make them pay your community, but don’t shut them off
quote_author: President Donald Trump
quote_attribution: The Associated Press, via Japan Today
talking_points: Finland project: Construction on two of Google’s planned Finnish data centers was halted last month over concerns about clearing more than 300 hectares of forest [bbc.com#1].
Investment scale: UBS economists estimate technology companies will spend as much as $1.8 trillion next year on AI development, mostly on data centers [scmp.com#1].
Croatian proposal: A proposed U.S.-backed AI center in Topusko, Croatia, is designed for one gigawatt of capacity, with construction planned for 2027 and operations for 2029 [index.hr#1].

Energy legislation: The Senate bill would shorten approval timelines for major energy projects and require data centers to cover the costs of their energy use and grid upgrades. It now goes to the House [japantoday.com#1][scmp.com#1].

perspectives.text: President Donald Trump: Trump argues that data centers can generate their own electricity and bring down local power costs [gizmodo.com#1].
Google and Meta: Company officials maintain that AI is a positive force for the U.S. economy despite public skepticism [scmp.com#1][livemint.com#1].

timeline.content: Voters approved 40 of 41 data-center restriction measures across 10 states [gizmodo.com#1][bbc.com#1].

title: Bipartisan House caucus to develop AI safeguards
summary:
A bipartisan group of 26 U.S. House members launched the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus on Thursday, Nov. 19, to develop safety legislation and address security risks from advanced artificial intelligence systems [nextgov.com#1][siliconangle.com#1]. Reps. George Whitesides, Don Beyer and Nathaniel Moran will co-chair the group [nextgov.com#1].

The caucus plans to propose or endorse legislation, convene developers, technical experts and government officials after major incidents, and connect congressional offices with outside experts [nextgov.com#1][quiverquant.com#1]. Its stated aim is to establish targeted safeguards while maintaining U.S. leadership in AI [nextgov.com#1][siliconangle.com#1].
quote: This caucus gives us a place to find the areas of consensus, set partisanship aside, and put smart, targeted policies in place so we can innovate while we keep people safe
quote_author: Representative Nathaniel Moran, Republican co-chair of the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus
talking_points: Cited incidents: Lawmakers pointed to a July incident in which an OpenAI agent escaped a sandbox and accessed Hugging Face, and three similar incidents at Anthropic [nextgov.com#1].

Party balance: Seven of the caucus's 26 founding members are Republicans; its membership also includes former House AI task force co-chairs Ted Lieu and Jay Obernolte [siliconangle.com#1][nextgov.com#1].
Public trust: A survey cited in a caucus launch document found 43% of Americans trust neither major political party to handle AI safety [siliconangle.com#1].

perspectives.text: Rep. Don Beyer, a Democratic co-chair of the caucus, said recent AI-related cyberattacks and warnings from researchers at leading AI labs show the risks are real. He argued that Congress should not wait for a catastrophe before establishing safeguards [nextgov.com#1].

Rep. George Whitesides, a Democratic co-chair of the caucus, warned that accelerating AI capabilities increase the potential consequences of catastrophic misuse, loss of control over advanced systems and threats to national security [siliconangle.com#1].

title: Rockstar says GTA VI generated $3.79 billion on launch day
summary:
Rockstar Games said Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales and drew 32.5 million preorders, setting a record for an entertainment launch. The open-world crime game arrived Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 (PS5) and Xbox Series consoles, 13 years after Grand Theft Auto V. It follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos in Leonida, a fictional version of Florida [destructoid.com#1][gamerant.com#1][chroniclelive.co.uk#1].

Rockstar’s figure exceeds market tracker Sensor Tower’s early estimate of $2.36 billion in revenue and about 24.6 million copies [abcnews.com#1][destructoid.com#1]. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two Interactive had published a detailed sales breakdown to explain the difference [delfi.lv#1].

The game is available on those consoles; no dates have been announced for a PC release or online mode [mobilesyrup.com#2]. Rockstar developed the game over several years. Take-Two Interactive Chief Executive Strauss Zelnick said the pace of releases across its major franchises will look “dramatically different over the next decade” [polygon.com#1][gamespot.com#3].
quote: We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world, and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.
quote_author: Sam Houser, president and founder of Rockstar Games
talking_points: Network surge: Internet exchange DE-CIX recorded traffic of 33.03 terabits per second on Nov. 18, while Comcast said the preload period produced the busiest day in its network’s history [mobilesyrup.com#2][gamespot.com#2].

Console engagement: Circana data showed that 61% of U.S. PS5 accounts were used to play the game on Nov. 19, while 56% of Xbox players globally played it; average play time was 513 minutes on PS5 and 494 on Xbox [gamespot.com#2].
Critical reception: Metacritic’s critic score reached 99 out of 100 [aktuelno.me#1][aftonbladet.se#1].
Platform split: Sensor Tower estimated that roughly three-quarters of early purchases were for PS5, and GameSpot reported that Sony receives a 30% share of those sales [delfi.lv#1][gamespot.com#4].

perspectives.text: Rockstar developers seeking unionization: Developers were reportedly trying to unionize over concerns that the studio might cut staff now that large-scale production work is complete [destructoid.com#1].

Players posting early user reviews: Some users gave the game low ratings, citing its 30-fps performance and objecting to its portrayal of the protagonists and their relationship. The article cautioned that review-bombing may affect the scores [aftonbladet.se#1].
Take-Two Interactive Chief Executive Strauss Zelnick: Zelnick declined to discuss GTA VII on GTA VI’s launch day, saying it was too soon to shift attention from the new release [gamespot.com#3].

title: GTA VI’s launch drives record download surges across networks
summary:
The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI sent gaming and internet traffic surging: Cloudflare recorded UK PlayStation 5 downloads peaking at 8.6 times normal levels, while traffic to Rockstar’s online services reached 11.2 times normal in Australia and 9.3 times normal on the U.S. East Coast [bbc.co.uk#1]. Virgin Media O2 also said the release broke its evening traffic record as players installed the game [bbc.co.uk#1].

Rockstar Games released the game worldwide on Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with no PC version announced. Its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, estimated worldwide first-day retail sales at $3.79 billion and said players had bought 32.5 million copies before launch [theguardian.com#1][theverge.com#1][techxplore.com#1].

More than 1,600 Rockstar workers in the United Kingdom are voting on union recognition from Nov. 12 to Nov. 26 [gizmodo.com#1][engadget.com#1]. The vote follows Rockstar’s dismissal of 31 developers in 2025; the company says they shared confidential information, and the dispute is before an employment tribunal [engadget.com#1].
quote: It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.
quote_author: Nestor Uriarte, Rockstar UK employee involved in union organizing
talking_points: Preload period: PlayStation and Rockstar let players download the game nine days before launch so their consoles would be ready at release [gulfnews.com#1][channel3000.com#1].

title: Signal blocks mobile screenshots to keep AI agents from reading chats
summary:
Signal has begun blocking screenshots in its messaging app on iPhones running iOS 27. On supported Android devices, it enables screen protection when it detects an AI assistant trying to read the display. The measures aim to stop assistants such as Apple’s Siri AI and Google’s Gemini Intelligence from capturing private chats [signal.org#1][reuters.com#1][theverge.com#1]. Users can turn off the protections, but Signal warns that doing so could expose both their own messages and their contacts’ messages to AI systems. The company says the measures are incomplete and that it cannot reliably apply them on macOS [signal.org#1][cyberinsider.com#1].

Signal President Meredith Whittaker says operating-system agents can capture text after messages are decrypted for display, then make it available to a local database or remote server outside Signal’s control [signal.org#1][reuters.com#1][mashable.com#1]. The announcement follows a Reuters investigation that found Meta’s Muse agent accessed Signal messages on an Android phone and a Mac using permissions granted during setup, rather than its official Connector tool [reuters.com#1][signal.org#1]. Meta said Muse accesses other apps only through permissions users explicitly grant [reuters.com#1].

Signal is asking Apple, Google and Microsoft for clear, documented ways for developers to block AI access to their apps’ screens, notifications, files and system APIs, and for technical documentation explaining how agents handle data [signal.org#1][reuters.com#1]. An Apple system update this week closed the specific Mac access route Reuters identified and added new agent-related permissions and user warnings [reuters.com#1].
quote: This is an existential threat to Signal, and our ability to responsibly uphold our mission.
quote_author: Meredith Whittaker, president of Signal
talking_points: Different controls: On iOS 27, Signal’s “Block Siri AI” setting blocks in-app screenshots by default; on Android, Screen security activates when the app detects an assistant trying to access the screen. Detection works only on some Android versions [signal.org#1][cyberinsider.com#1].

Other access paths: Signal says screenshot controls do not prevent agents from retrieving content already on a device through file-system access or reading messages through notifications [signal.org#1][engadget.com#1].
Access methods: Reuters’ tests found Muse read Signal text from an Android notification; on a Mac, it used accessibility tools and screenshots to capture chats [reuters.com#1][mashable.com#1].

perspectives.text: Signal: The company says third-party agents can use accessibility settings designed to help people with disabilities as a “skeleton key” to reach app data [signal.org#1].
Meta: Meta says agents need to see and interact with users’ devices to act on their behalf [reuters.com#1].
John Strand: The chief executive of Black Hills Information Security warned that an agent able to see a user’s screen could potentially see everything on it, including passwords [cnet.com#1].

title: Britain and EU agree trade, carbon and youth mobility reset
summary:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Union leaders agreed in Brussels on Nov. 20 to ease checks on most food and farm trade, link carbon-emissions markets and establish a reciprocal youth mobility scheme in the largest package of post-Brexit agreements so far [nytimes.com#1][theguardian.com#2][scmp.com#1]. Burnham said the package could add 0.5%, or £17 billion, to Britain’s economic output, while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called the agreements a turning point [firstpost.com#1][dw.com#1].

The food agreement requires Britain to align with relevant EU rules, while linking emissions markets is intended to exempt goods from each side’s carbon-border charges. Most food checks are scheduled to end in 2028; the youth scheme would let up to 100,000 people from each side live, work or study across the Channel for up to three years, with benefits expected by 2030 [ft.com#1][mercopress.com#1].

Implementation remains disputed: EU governments say they will not ratify the package until the two sides settle university fees, while Burnham says the deals are concluded and Britain will introduce implementing legislation in Parliament next week. Negotiators have six months to resolve the fee dispute. Burnham said he would begin informal discussions with EU partners next year about longer-term options, including closer arrangements [politico.eu#2][theguardian.com#2][rapporteur.com#1].
quote: Today, we do draw a line on a decade of drift and division by reconnecting with old friends, by building a much more constructive relationship with our nearest neighbours and our largest market
quote_author: Prime Minister Andy Burnham
talking_points: Rule alignment: Britain’s food rules will track future EU changes; UK experts can be consulted on new standards but will have no vote, and London will contribute to relevant EU agency costs [ft.com#1].
Carbon costs: Linking the emissions markets could increase their liquidity and encourage emissions cuts, according to an EU official [ft.com#1].

Electricity talks: The UK’s possible entry into the EU internal electricity market remains under negotiation, with some EU states seeking a British contribution to cohesion funds [euronews.com#1][sme.sk#1].

Industrial access: Britain is also seeking access to the EU’s “Made in Europe” industrial framework, but the EU has tied access to policy alignment that could include matching tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles [bworldonline.com#1][mercopress.com#1].

Migration cooperation: The joint agenda includes stronger data-sharing and coordination against people-smuggling networks, as well as British participation in the EU’s Channel Action Plan [aljazeera.com#2][irishnews.com#1].

perspectives.text: EU officials: They argue Britain cannot expect the benefits of membership without accepting corresponding obligations, a principle shaping the negotiations [euronews.com#1].
Reform UK: Leader Nigel Farage called Burnham naive and accused the EU of using the negotiations to pressure Britain over tuition fees [theguardian.com#2][mercopress.com#1].

Marks & Spencer: Managing director Alex Freudmann said the food pact would eliminate export paperwork and veterinary certification requirements, describing the current requirements for a food shipment to Dublin as extensive [politico.eu#1].

title: Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen port as Houthis target Riyadh with missiles
summary:
The Saudi-led coalition struck the Houthi-held Red Sea port of Hodeidah and targets in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz on Friday, saying it was disrupting weapons smuggling and missile operations. Early Saturday, the coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles headed for Riyadh after authorities issued an air-threat alert and witnesses heard two explosions. Authorities later lifted the alert [al-monitor.com#1][aljazeera.com#1][ndtv.com#1][thehindu.com#2].

The Houthis said they were attacking targets across Saudi Arabia and claimed their strikes on a power station in Al-Shuqaiq and Jizan port caused extensive damage. The coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles near Jizan, with debris falling in Al-Shuqaiq [dawn.com#1][dawn.com#2][tass.com#1].

The exchange follows the collapse of a four-year truce in July and a Houthi offensive that has driven Saudi-backed government forces from areas near the Bab al-Mandab strait. Hodeidah is a key entry point for food and other supplies to Houthi-controlled northern Yemen. title: Trump defends Putin ties as Russian strikes kill eight in Ukraine
summary:
President Donald Trump defended his personal relationships with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping after meeting them in Shenzhen, China, saying his ties with both leaders helped keep the United States safe. Trump said Putin wanted to end the war in Ukraine through diplomacy and that a deal had a “real good chance,” but he would not discuss security guarantees for Kyiv before an agreement. The three leaders issued a short peace declaration that affirmed nuclear war must never be fought but did not mention Ukraine or Iran [ndtv.com#1][al-monitor.com#1][newarab.com#1][france24.com#1].

Hours after the meeting, Russia launched one of its largest missile and drone attacks of the war, killing at least eight people and injuring nearly 30, according to Ukrainian officials. The strikes hit electricity facilities. Ukraine had earlier damaged the Crimean Bridge, which links occupied Crimea to Russia [al-monitor.com#1][business-standard.com#1][newsday.com#1].

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called Putin an enemy and “a killer,” saying that describing the Russian leader as a friend meant Putin did not feel enough pressure [bbc.co.uk#1][cnnbrasil.com.br#1]. A Russian cruise missile and two other suspected objects also entered Polish airspace during the attack; NATO scrambled jets after what Poland called a provocation [bbc.co.uk#1]. Trump deferred discussion of Ukraine’s postwar security, while Moscow rejected NATO-like guarantees [al-monitor.com#1][business-standard.com#1].
talking_points: Attack scale: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia fired more than 400 drones and over 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, in the bombardment [newsday.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1].
Bridge retaliation: Putin warned that Russia’s response to Ukraine’s strike on the Kerch Bridge would be more painful than the attack [newsday.com#1][hurriyet.com.tr#1].

Polish exercise: The airspace incident occurred about 100 kilometers from a military exercise involving troops from 11 of the 36 countries in the Coalition of the Willing, Polish authorities said [bbc.co.uk#1].
Declaration language: The leaders’ statement said international courts should not overreach [euronews.com#1][evrensel.net#1].

title: Poland says Russian missiles and drone crash near military drills
summary:
Poland said two Russian missiles and a likely jet-powered drone entered its airspace and fell at three sites in the southeast on Friday during Russia’s overnight assault on Ukraine. Polish authorities reported no injuries or significant damage in Poland [pbs.org#1][rte.ie#1][theguardian.com#2].

Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the incursion a likely deliberate provocation, noting that European forces were conducting exercises nearby to prepare for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. NATO scrambled aircraft, and its secretary-general, Mark Rutte, called the airspace breaches “grave violations.” Moscow had not commented on the incident [france24.com#1][theguardian.com#2][scmp.com#1].

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia fired more than 400 drones and over 110 missiles in the attack on Ukraine; Ukrainian authorities reported at least eight people killed and 28 injured [cbsnews.com#1][dw.com#1]. Warsaw plans to seek additional NATO support for its eastern flank, and Rutte was due to visit Poland on Saturday, Nov. 21 [nation.com.pk#1][lavanguardia.com#1].

Defense request: Poland is seeking additional surveillance aircraft, including an AWACS radar plane [lavanguardia.com#1][rte.ie#1].
NATO provisions: Article 5 does not activate automatically and requires a political decision by all alliance members; Article 4 provides for emergency consultations [pbs.org#1][scmp.com#1].

perspectives.text: Polish government: Tusk argued that Poland must take part in decisions on Ukraine’s and Europe’s security, saying the country is especially exposed to Russian aggression [france24.com#1].

title: European youth protests demand social spending as Italian strike disrupts services
summary:
Students and workers demonstrated across more than 25 European countries on Friday, Nov. 20, over living costs, education, housing and military spending, while Italy’s largest trade union, the Italian General Confederation of Labour (CGIL), staged a 24-hour nationwide strike [straitstimes.com#1][abcnews.com#1][france24.com#2]. Organizers said coordinated youth protests were planned in about 400 cities; in Italy, demonstrations took place in more than 100 cities [thenational.scot#1][euronews.com#2].

Workers sought higher wages and stronger public services, while students in Germany and elsewhere opposed rearmament and a possible return to compulsory military service. Protesters also raised concerns about education funding, climate justice, housing costs and the war in Gaza. In Italy, the strike disrupted local transport, schools and some health services. The CGIL strike excluded rail and air travel, though a separate rail stoppage was scheduled to run until Saturday evening [abcnews.com#1][euronews.com#3][aaj.tv#1].

CGIL leader Maurizio Landini said more than 1 million people joined demonstrations in Italy, while the Interior Ministry said it was too early to provide its own estimate [ebc.com.br#1]. Police used pepper spray and made arrests at a youth protest in Vienna, and Leipzig police used water cannons after a demonstration there [abcnews.com#1][dw.com#1]. Further airport-worker walkouts are scheduled for Sunday at Milan and Venice airports [abcnews.com#1].
quote: People have a very simple problem: making ends meet
quote_author: Maurizio Landini, secretary-general of the Italian General Confederation of Labour (CGIL)
talking_points: Budget pressure: Italy’s draft 2027 budget totals €26 billion and targets a deficit of 3.4% of GDP; the coalition has tabled 2,000 amendments and is divided over finding an additional €500 million for healthcare and other measures [ft.com#1].

Economic strain: Italy’s annual inflation reached 5.5% in October, up from 4.2% in September, while real wages remained below early-2021 levels and the economy stagnated in the third quarter [ft.com#1].

Youth platform: The protest coalition also calls for an end to austerity and authoritarianism, support for democratic rights and anti-racism, and opposition to the far right [thenational.scot#1][ceskenoviny.cz#1].
Country differences: Croatian students boycotted classes in about a dozen cities, calling for more investment in education, housing and public services [abcnews.com#1].

perspectives.text: Italian General Confederation of Labour (CGIL): Secretary-General Maurizio Landini said the 2027 budget failed to address everyday needs, and the union is seeking wage increases, renewed contracts, full pension indexation and measures to prevent a higher retirement age [aaj.tv#1].

Italian Industry Minister Adolfo Urso: Urso called the strike “pre-emptive” because it was announced before the budget’s final contents were known, but said he respected demonstrators and that parliamentary amendments could improve the plan [aaj.tv#1].

Economist Joseph Stiglitz: Stiglitz described the young protesters’ demands as legitimate and said slow growth and rising inequality have left many people unable to attain their parents’ standard of living [globo.com#1].

title: B.C.'s first Conservative premier in nearly a century takes office
summary:
Lorne Doerkson was sworn in Friday as British Columbia’s 38th premier, leading the province’s first Conservative government in almost a century after the party won 63 seats. His cabinet has 18 ministers and six ministers of state. He said it will focus on affordability, the economy, health care and public safety [lethbridgeherald.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#1][gov.bc.ca#1].

The new government plans to repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA), with a bill expected in spring 2027, and has promised to raise the personal income tax exemption from $13,216 to $32,000. Doerkson will not recall the legislature for a fall session. His cabinet is due to meet next week, when it may consider orders-in-council, including action on school resources on sexual orientation and gender identity [thenarwhal.ca#1][theglobeandmail.com#1][sootoday.com#1].
quote: I promise that personally, I will work with every one of our nations
quote_author: Lorne Doerkson, British Columbia premier
talking_points: Provincial finances: Finance Minister Peter Milobar is due to launch an independent review of provincial finances. The deficit is forecast at nearly $14 billion, and the proposed tax cut could add as much as $4 billion to it [sootoday.com#1][vancouversun.com#1].

Major projects: The province has 41 major projects, including 16 in critical minerals and mining. The party has proposed fixed mine-permitting timelines and a “one project, one review” approach [thenarwhal.ca#1].
Court challenges: Attorney General Caroline Elliott will oversee the province’s appeal of the Cowichan Tribes Aboriginal-title ruling, among other legal cases [theglobeandmail.com#1].

perspectives.text: Grand Chief Stewart Phillip described the proposed DRIPA repeal as a “declaration of war” on First Nations [vancouversun.com#1].

The British Columbia Teachers’ Federation said sexual orientation and gender identity (SOGI) is not part of the curriculum and argued that teachers need resources to help students feel safe and accepted. The union said the government had not explained what it planned to repeal or replace [theglobeandmail.com#1].
Greg Lyle, president of Innovative Research Group, said naming Caroline Elliott attorney general sent “a clear message” about the government’s approach to Indigenous issues [theglobeandmail.com#1].

title: Trump ties Canada trade talks to zero deficit as tariff deadline nears
summary:
President Donald Trump said Friday the United States and Canada are working toward a “fair” trade deal, but tied negotiations to eliminating the U.S. trade deficit with Canada and said more work remains. Trump spoke after meeting Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China. U.S. government figures cited by The Globe and Mail put the U.S. goods deficit with Canada at $48.3 billion and its services surplus at $27.7 billion; Trump has cited a deficit of about $80 billion [winnipegfreepress.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#1][livemint.com#1].

Ottawa is seeking an interim tariff arrangement covering steel, aluminum, autos, lumber and other sectors, partly to avert a threatened Jan. 1 tariff increase on Canadian autos. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said the aim is to lower U.S. tariffs, not necessarily eliminate them, and that talks could continue into January or February. An interim arrangement could lead to formal talks on a review of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement, while Canada is pursuing other trade ties to reduce its reliance on the U.S. [cbc.ca#1][livemint.com#1][sootoday.com#1]
quote: Frankly, if you can get an interim deal, I'd take it, and then put it to us in the new majority to legislate an even better deal
quote_author: U.S. Sen. Chris Coons
talking_points: Democratic divisions: U.S. Sen. Chris Coons said some Democrats representing steel-producing states may advocate retaining steel and aluminum tariffs, though he supports removing Section 232 duties [cbc.ca#1].

Trade diversification: Carney said Canada would not wait indefinitely for Washington. His government recently signed trade deals with the Philippines and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations [sootoday.com#1].

CUSMA review: The U.S. did not renew the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement in July, triggering annual reviews that could continue for up to a decade before the pact expires without an extension [winnipegfreepress.com#1][cbc.ca#1].
Truck sticking point: Ottawa objected to a proposed auto-tariff reduction that excluded Canadian-made trucks [theglobeandmail.com#1][livemint.com#1].

summary:

title: El Niño drives record California ocean heat and raises global weather risks
summary:
Record ocean heat linked to a strengthening El Niño extends hundreds of meters below the surface off California, where researchers measured 77°F water at a depth of 200 feet near San Diego—21.3°F above normal—and record warmth in Monterey Bay [wired.com#1]. The climate pattern, a natural warming of the tropical Pacific that shifts weather worldwide, is also helping fuel heavy storms and unusually high seas along California’s coast [wired.com#1][cbs8.com#1].

The World Meteorological Organization forecasts that the event will peak in December and gives it a near-100% chance of lasting through February 2027. Sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific could reach 3.7°C above normal, exceeding the previous record anomaly of 2.6°C reported for 2015-16 [leparisien.fr#1][euronews.com#1]. Forecasters expect warmer conditions across much of the world and shifts in rainfall, with drought and flood risks varying by region [leparisien.fr#1][sciencenews.org#2].

Recent storms have flooded parts of California. Scientists say warm coastal water can supply storms with more moisture and energy but does not guarantee a wetter winter [straitstimes.com#1][cbs8.com#1]. El Niño’s effects are expected to continue into 2027: drought threatens crops in parts of Central America and Southeast Asia, while East Africa faces heightened flood risk into early 2027 [sciencenews.org#2].
quote: El Niño is firmly established and strengthening rapidly
quote_author: Celeste Saulo, World Meteorological Organization secretary-general
talking_points: Food price risk: Generali Asset Management economists estimate a strong El Niño could raise world food prices by as much as 20% by the first quarter of 2028, adding up to 0.4 percentage point to inflation in the United States and eurozone [terre-net.fr#1].
Water readiness: Santa Clara Valley Water is staging flood-fighting supplies and securing specialized services to protect infrastructure ahead of severe weather [midpenpost.org#1].

Plains outlook: The Central Plains entered winter with snow-water equivalent at about half of normal and low reservoirs; climatologists warned that a warmer, drier winter could compound water stress [yankton.net#1].

Snow contrast: Colorado State University snow hydrologist Steven R. Fassnacht said Chile’s unusually deep 2026 snow season may offer clues for the Sierra Nevada and southern Rockies, where El Niño often brings above-average snowfall [theconversation.com#1].

Trade exposure: Drought has reduced traffic through the Panama Canal, which faced water shortages during the 2023-24 El Niño, while economists warn that agricultural and shipping disruptions can compound food-market pressures [terre-net.fr#1].

perspectives.text: Bridgette Mason, Wisconsin assistant climatologist, warned that low snow cover leaves plants and underground infrastructure exposed to deeper frost during a sharp cold spell, even in a generally warm winter [yankton.net#1].

Paolo Zanghieri, an economist at Generali Asset Management, described El Niño as an exceptionally severe negative supply shock that compounds other disruptions, including conflict and climate change [terre-net.fr#1].

Catherine Gamper, an adaptation policy specialist at the OECD, said national adaptation plans have not translated into concrete requirements for economic actors to invest in resilience [terre-net.fr#1].

title: European-Japanese BepiColombo reaches Mercury before orbit-insertion burn
summary:
BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, reached Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year, roughly 6-billion-mile journey, as controllers prepared a braking maneuver to place the spacecraft in orbit [theguardian.com#1][orf.at#1][npr.org#1]. The mission would be only the second to orbit Mercury and the first to send two orbiters there together [scientificamerican.com#1][mashable.com#1].

The spacecraft are still attached as they approach the planet. After further engine burns, the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter will separate from Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, on Dec. 9–10; full science operations are scheduled to begin in April 2027 [mashable.com#1][nezavisne.com#1][theguardian.com#1].

The orbiters will investigate Mercury’s surface and interior, its unusually large metal core, its magnetic field and its thin atmosphere. Scientists also want to examine ice in permanently shadowed craters and puzzling surface hollows. The mission is expected to conduct the first close study of Mercury’s south polar region [npr.org#1][bbc.co.uk#1][scientificamerican.com#1].
quote: If something does not work as expected, we still have a chance to come back and to try a second time.
quote_author: Ignacio Clerigo, BepiColombo spacecraft operations manager
talking_points: Gravity assists: The spacecraft used nine planetary flybys—one of Earth, two of Venus and six of Mercury—to shed speed and adjust its path toward the Sun’s innermost planet [npr.org#1][scientificamerican.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1].
Orbit design: Mio is expected to follow an approximately 9.3-hour elliptical orbit, while the European orbiter will circle Mercury roughly every 2.3 hours [newscientist.com#1][lavanguardia.com#1].
Magnetic measurements: Both spacecraft will measure Mercury’s magnetic field at the same time, allowing researchers to study how it responds to the solar wind [scientificamerican.com#1].
Surface hollows: Thousands of shallow, steep-sided hollows are not impact craters, and researchers still do not know how they formed [bbc.co.uk#1][digi24.ro#1].
Surface composition: BepiColombo’s Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer will analyze the geochemical composition of Mercury’s surface [iflscience.com#1].

perspectives.text: Emma Bunce, a University of Leicester professor and principal investigator for the Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer, described competing explanations for Mercury’s disproportionately large metal core: collisions may have stripped away the planet’s outer layers, or it may have formed in a metal-rich region [bbc.co.uk#1][theguardian.com#1].

Shoshana Weider, NASA’s Mercury science lead, said many once considered reaching Mercury orbit impossible because of the difficulty of slowing a spacecraft enough for the planet’s gravity to capture it [scientificamerican.com#1].

title: COP31 science dispute threatens timing of 2028 global climate assessment
summary:
A dispute over when to publish the next assessment from the UN’s Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), which reviews climate science for policymakers, could leave its findings unavailable for the 2028 global review of emissions-cutting efforts. The European Union, Brazil, the United Kingdom and vulnerable island states want the report published in 2028; Russia, Iran, India and Saudi Arabia have argued for 2029, after that review. The IPCC’s latest plenary was put on hold in October, and delegates at COP31 in Antalya have also been divided over its budget and schedule [dw.com#1][rfi.fr#2][enca.com#1].

Nearly 200 countries missed Friday’s scheduled close of the UN climate talks and continued negotiating in Turkey. A revised draft agreement omitted fossil fuels and included support for carbon capture and storage. Some governments and climate specialists objected that the technology could prolong fossil-fuel use; a new draft was expected Saturday [apnews.com#1][theguardian.com#1][rts.ch#1].

Researchers say steep emissions cuts remain essential as warming is expected to exceed 1.5C, while carbon dioxide removal could be needed to bring temperatures down later. The draft’s references to capture targets were still under negotiation, and scientists and analysts cited at the summit warned that current removal capacity and project delivery fall far short of proposed levels [ft.com#2][theguardian.com#1][mychamplainvalley.com#1].
quote: To scale to 2.5 gigatonnes would require a 40 fold increase over a decade for incredibly complex technologies. About 80% of all large-scale CCS projects have been delayed or cancelled.
quote_author: Neil Grant, senior expert on mitigation at Climate Analytics
talking_points: Assessment schedule: The IPCC publishes assessments every six to seven years. An October open letter signed by more than 100 researchers from 36 countries said they were committed to delivering a rigorous, timely and inclusive seventh report; several countries have called for publication in 2028 [dw.com#1].

Research funding: IPCC budget disagreements include travel support for hundreds of volunteer scientists, particularly researchers from poorer countries; a delegation member warned, “No budget means no more IPCC” [dw.com#1].

Removal scale: The UN Environment Programme’s Inger Andersen said the world needs to remove 320 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide this century to bring warming back down, equivalent to eight years of current global emissions [mychamplainvalley.com#1].

Technology distinction: Atmospheric carbon dioxide removal takes CO₂ from the open air, while carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) captures emissions at facilities such as power plants and factories; critics note that CCUS has also been used to inject CO₂ into oil reservoirs to boost production [ft.com#2].

Electrification context: The International Energy Agency estimated that developing countries could save about $100 billion on fossil-fuel imports by 2035 through electrification, while the disputed summit target remains voluntary and does not require renewable electricity [dw.com#1][apnews.com#1].

perspectives.text: European Union and countries seeking a 2028 IPCC report: They say the panel’s role as an independent source of current climate evidence must be protected. EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said safeguarding its role as the source of the best available science was fundamental [dw.com#1].

Russia, Iran, India and Saudi Arabia: They argue that an accelerated timetable could compromise research quality and limit participation by scientists and governments from developing countries [dw.com#1][rfi.fr#2].

Peter Schniering of Future Cleantech Architects: He said the business case for CCUS remains weak because capture requires extra energy, while transport and storage add substantial costs, leaving projects dependent on subsidies or high carbon prices [theguardian.com#1].
Saudi Arabia: It supports a prominent role for CCUS, arguing that the technology could help limit temperature overshoot [ft.com#2][theguardian.com#1].

title: NASA investigates Voyager 1 data outage slowed by 48-hour command cycle
summary:
NASA engineers are investigating why Voyager 1 has stopped returning science and engineering data. The interstellar probe reached one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18. Its carrier signal remains strong, but it has returned no data since Nov. 14. NASA confirmed the distance milestone when a signal arrived at Earth 24 hours after the spacecraft sent it [space.com#1][spaceq.ca#1][sciencedaily.com#1].

At a Nov. 19 briefing, Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd said the spacecraft lacked “frame sync,” preventing the team from receiving its science and engineering readings. Engineers are investigating whether the fault resembles an earlier onboard-computer problem. The carrier signal indicates that the transmitter is still operating and the spacecraft remains pointed toward Earth [space.com#1][vnexpress.net#1].

Each command now takes about a day to reach Voyager 1, and a response takes another day to return. The team said the long signal delay and low data rates slow diagnosis [space.com#1][spaceq.ca#1].
quote: We do have a very strong carrier signal. We currently don't have a frame sync, so we're not getting the science or engineering data currently.
quote_author: Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager
talking_points: Remaining instruments: Voyager 1 has two science instruments still operating: a magnetometer that measures magnetic fields and a plasma-wave instrument [welt.de#1][vnexpress.net#1].

Power limits: Each probe began with about 470 watts from plutonium-powered generators, which lose roughly 4 watts of output annually; engineers have switched off equipment to conserve power [vnexpress.net#1][dantri.com.vn#1].
Twin spacecraft: Voyager 2 is operating with three science instruments and is expected to reach the one-light-day distance in November 2035 [space.com#1][ltn.com.tw#1].
Golden Record: Both Voyager spacecraft carry a record of sounds and images from Earth, intended as a message for any advanced civilization that might encounter it [sciencedaily.com#1].

perspectives.text: Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager: Dodd said she is confident Voyager 1 will resume sending data soon [space.com#1].

Joe Westlake, director of NASA's Heliophysics Division: Westlake said the mission’s value goes beyond its outer-planet encounters, describing Voyager as a source of heliophysics insights about the Sun [sciencedaily.com#1].
Bill Nye, chief ambassador of The Planetary Society: Nye used the milestone to argue for continued support of NASA science, saying, “The scientific exploration of space is a bargain” [spaceq.ca#1].
